title: Network Delay Time
summary: Given a network with n nodes labeled 1 to n and travel times for directed edges, determine the minimum time for a signal to reach all nodes starting from node k.
statement: Given a network with n nodes labeled 1 to n and travel times for directed edges, determine the minimum time for a signal to reach all nodes starting from node k. If full coverage is impossible, return -1.
constraints: 1 <= k <= n <= 100; directed nonnegative weighted edges are unique.
Return the earliest time all nodes receive the signal, or -1 if any is unreachable.
hints: The next unsettled node with smallest known arrival time can never be improved by a nonnegative edge.
Run Dijkstra from the starting node and settle each node once.
Pop (time,node); skip settled nodes; push time+weight for outgoing edges; take maximum settled time.
Dijkstra proves settled distances are shortest, and their maximum is exactly when the last reachable node receives the signal.
editorial: Dijkstra proves settled distances are shortest, and their maximum is exactly when the last reachable node receives the signal.

tests.explanation: Shortest arrival times are one, zero, one, and two, so all nodes receive by time two.
Node one is unreachable from node two, so the answer is -1.
